headline: Approved nine entertainment and alcohol permits for events in September through November; summoned The Cellar and Monica McNamara.
summary: Jacqueline Wehtje spoke against the Noche de Lares permit, which was still approved. The Cellar was summoned to the October 5, 2026 meeting after an August 22 incident involving multiple patrons and a possible overservice and public safety issue.
decisions: Approved minutes of the September 3, 2026 regular and executive meetings, 3-0.
Approved two entertainment permits for Fitchburg State homecoming events on November 7, 2026, 3-0.
Approved Noche de Lares entertainment permit for September 23, 2026, 3-0.
Approved amended entertainment permit for BAM Festival on September 26, 2026, with end time moved to 5:30 PM, 3-0.
Approved Employee Appreciation Party entertainment permit for October 8, 2026, 3-0.
Approved Zach's Goal Washer Tournament entertainment permit for September 27, 2026, 3-0.
Approved St. Bernard's High School 5k and Fun Walk entertainment permit for October 4, 2026, 3-0.
Approved amended all-alcoholic beverages permit for Zach's Goal Washer Tournament on September 27, 2026, 3-0.
Approved wine and malt beverages permit for Employee Appreciation Party on October 8, 2026, 3-0.
Approved summons of The Cellar to the October 5, 2026 meeting, 3-0.
Approved summons of Ms. Monica McNamara to discuss pocket license, 3-0.

Page 1 
 
Monty Tech                    BOARD OF LICENSE COMMISSIONERS 
         City Hall, 718 Main Street 
              Fitchburg MA  01420 
              (978) 829-1820    
  
Daniel Sarefield, Chairman        
Richard Boscardin 
Glenn Fossa 
MINUTES OF MEETING 
A regular meeting of the Board of License Commissioners was held on Monday, September 14, 2026, called to 
order by Commissioner Sarefield at 6:00 PM. Commissioner Boscardin and Commissioner Fossa were present 
VIA zoom. FPD Liaison Lt. Christopher Bellofatto was present and Officer Michael Sevigny. City Clerk Joanna 
Bilotta and Assistant City Clerk Elizabeth McNiff were present.  
I. REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF PRIOR MEETING(S) 
Regular Minutes and Executive Minutes of September 3, 2026.  
The regular and executive minutes of September 3, 2026 were approved by roll call vote 3/0.  
 
II. NEW APPLICATIONS 
Please note that the Commission may enter into Executive Session pursuant to G.L. c. 30A, sec. 21(a) 
(5) (Discussion of CORI results), if required during this portion of the agenda, and will return to 
regular session upon completion. 
 
 Monday – Sat urday Entertainment Permit  
Shane Franzen, Fitchburg State Homecoming Carnival, 1 Ross Street, Saturday November 7, 2026, 
from 4:00 PM – 11:00 PM, for DJ and carnival rides, for approximately 1000.   
Tanya Crowley, Fitchburg State Homecoming Tailgate, 1000 John Fitch Hwy, Civic Center Parking 
Lot, Saturday November 7, 2026, from 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM, for DJ, for approximately 500.   
Mr. Franzen and Ms. Crowley were present at the meeting. Commissioner Sarefield noted for the 
record that while he is an employee at Fitchburg State University, he has no financial stake in these 
events. Commissioner Sarefield reviewed the applications and verified that Mr. Franzen and Ms. 
Crowley are aware that all entertainment must be shut down thirty minutes prior to closing. Mr. 
Franzen informed the commission this will be the same set up as years past and that Fitchburg State 
University Police will be present at the events.  
No concerns from Lt. Bellofatto. 
Applications approved by unanimous roll call vote 3/0.  
Diego Barahona, Noche de Lares, 46-50 Snow Street, Abolitionist Park, Wednesday, September 23, 
2026, from 4:00 PM – 7:00 PM, for live amplified music, for approximately 50 people  
Mr. Barahona was present at the meeting. Commissioner reviewed the application and verified that Mr. 
Barahona is aware that all entertainment must be shut down thirty minutes prior to closing. Fitchburg
Page 2 
resident Jacqueline Wehtje was present at the meeting and stated her opposition to this entertainment 
permit.  
No concerns from Lt. Bellofatto. 
Application approved by unanimous roll call vote 3/0.  
Achla Madan, 23rd Annual Fitchburg BAM Festival, 0 Boulder Drive, Riverfront Park, Saturday, 
September 26, 2026, from 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM, for live acoustic music and DJ, for approximately 
1500 people.  
Ms. Madan was present at the meeting. Commissioner Sarefield reviewed the application and verified 
that Ms. Madan is aware that all entertainment must be shut down thirty minutes prior to closing. Ms. 
Madan informed the commission this will be the same set up as years past. Ms. Madan asked to amend 
the end time to 5:30 PM.  
No concerns from Lt. Bellofatto. 
Amended application approved by unanimous roll call vote 3/0. 
Keith Poirier, 166 Boulder Drive, Employee Appreciation Party, Thursday, October 8, 2026 from 11:00 
AM PM to 4:00 PM, for DJ, for approximately 175 people.  
Ms. Mary Fritz a representative from the company was present at the meeting. Commissioner Sarefield 
reviewed the application and verified that Ms. Fritz is aware that all entertainment must be shut down 
thirty minutes prior to closing. Ms. Fritz informed the commission this will be the same set up as years 
past.  
No concerns from Lt. Bellofatto. 
Application approved by unanimous roll call vote 3/0. 
Sunday Entertainment Permit  
Katherine Marsh, Zach’s Goal Washer Tournament, 68 Airport Road, Sunday, September 27, 2026, 
from 12:00 PM – 5:30 PM, for live amplified music, for approximately 100 people.  
Ms. Marsh was present at the meeting. Commissioner Sarefield reviewed the application and verified 
that Ms. Marsh is aware that all entertainment must be shut down thirty minutes prior to closing. Ms. 
Marsh informed the commission this will be the same set up as years past.  
No concerns from Lt. Bellofatto. 
Application approved by unanimous roll call vote 3/0. 
Joanne Pagnotta, St. Bernard’s High School 5k and Fun Walk, 260 Summer Street, Sunday, October 4, 
2026, from 10:00 AM – 12:30 PM, for broadcast, for approximately 170 people.  
Commissioner Boscardin spoke on behalf of Ms. Pagnotta. Commissioner Sarefield reviewed the 
application and verified that Ms. Pagnotta is aware that all entertainment must be shut down thirty 
minutes prior to closing. Commissioner Boscardin confirmed that she is aware.  
No concerns from Lt. Bellofatto. 
Application approved by unanimous roll call vote 3/0. 
Special One Day All Alcoholic Beverages 
Aimee Murphy, Zach’s Goal Washer Tournament, 68 Airport Road, Sunday, September 27, 2026, from 
12:00 PM – 5:30 PM, for approximately 100 people.
Page 3 
Ms. Murphy was present at the meeting. Commissioner Sarefield reviewed the application and verified 
that the events will have TIP certified servers. Commissioner Sarefield stated that all serving of alcohol 
must be ceased thirty minutes prior to closing.  
 No concerns from Lt. Bellofatto.  
Amended application approved by unanimous roll call vote 3/0. 
Special One Day Wine & Malt Beverages 
Keith Poirier, 166 Boulder Drive, Employee Appreciation Party, Thursday, October 8, 2026 from 11:00 
AM PM to 4:00 PM, for approximately 175 people.  
Ms. Mary Fritz a representative from the company was present at the meeting. Commissioner Sarefield 
reviewed the application and verified that the events will have TIP certified servers. Commissioner 
Sarefield stated that all serving of alcohol must be ceased thirty minutes prior to closing. Ms. Fritz 
informed the commission this will be the same set up as years past.  
 No concerns from Lt. Bellofatto.  
Application approved by unanimous roll call vote 3/0. 
 
III. CORRESPONDENCE  
 City Clerk Joanna Bilotta shared correspondence received from Mr. and Mrs. Bujold on the status of the 
 status of Upper Common dba The Boulder, 880 Main Street.   
 Motion to summons in Ms. Monica McNamara to discuss pocket license approved by unanimous roll 
 call vote 3/0.  
 City Clerk Joanna Bilotta shared correspondence received f rom Ms. Wehtje regarding her opposition 
 on the entertainment for Diego Barahona.  
 On file at the City Clerk’s Office.  
 
IV. NEW BUSINESS 
  Lt.  Bellofatto shared with the commission an incident that took place at The Cellar on Saturday, 
 August 22, 2026 at approximately 1:5 3 AM. That involved multiple patrons with the possibility of 
 overservice and public safety issue.  
 Motion to summons The Ce llar to the Monday, October 5, 2026 meeting by unanimous roll call vote 
 3/0.
Page 4 
 
NEXT REGULAR MEETING 
 
 
Monday, October 5, 2026 
 
 
The meeting adjourned at 7:08 PM 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Joanna Bilotta, City Clerk
